title: Grow safely: buy together, delegate with controls, plan for risk

say: Grow safely: buy together, delegate with controls, and plan for risk.
This is the video for module three of Supply Chain and Raw Materials Sourcing: growing a resilient supply chain.
Each layer between you and the source adds a margin and a delay. Buying closer can lower your price, but needs bigger orders, more cash earlier, and more risk on your side.

say: Funke and four others each pay 2,500 naira per kg for 25 kg. A processor offers 2,150 naira per kg for 250 kg. Figures are illustrative.
The goods cost 537,500 naira, and transport for the whole load is 30,000 naira.
They share transport by weight: 30,000 divided by 250 is 120 naira per kg. So everyone's landed cost is 2,270 naira per kg, a saving of 230 naira.
Funke orders 80 kg and pays 181,600 naira, saving 18,400. Kemi orders 20 kg and pays 45,400.
The 567,500 naira collected exactly covers goods and transport, and each member saves about 9%.
Group money needs clear rules. Write a short agreement with the spec, each member's quantity, how costs are shared, and who holds the money.
Collect all money into one account before paying, and share receipts in the group. Weigh each share in front of members or on video, and agree in advance what happens if the material fails the spec.

panel.heading: Group buying rules
items: Collect all money first, into one account
Weigh each share on delivery, on video
Agree what happens if it fails the spec

say: Some materials are only available abroad. International trade uses Incoterms to state who pays and when risk passes. Always agree the term and the named place in writing. Under CIF, the seller pays freight, but risk still passes to you at loading.

panel.heading: Three risks when you import

cards.d: Agree the Incoterm and named place in writing. Under CIF, risk passes to you at loading.
A 10% weaker naira turned 3,000,000 naira of goods into 3,300,000 naira.
Check SON and NAFDAC rules, use a licensed customs agent, verify the supplier, start with a sample.

say: There is also exchange-rate risk. For illustration, goods costing 3,000,000 naira cost 3,300,000 if the naira weakens by 10% before you pay. Build a margin for this.

say: Some imports must meet SON or NAFDAC rules. Speak with a licensed customs agent first. Never pay a foreign supplier you have not verified, and start with a sample shipment.

say: Her senior tailor checks every delivery, and payment goes from the business account only after the receiving record is signed.
This is separation of duties. And anyone who buys for you must declare any personal link to a supplier, and report or refuse gifts.

say: Resilience means keeping production going when something goes wrong. Score each risk from 1 to 5 for likelihood and for impact, and multiply. 15 or more needs action now, 8 to 14 needs a plan, and below 8 you watch.

panel.heading: Score each risk: likelihood x impact

say: For Amaka, her only bottle distributor failing for two weeks scores 20. She qualifies a second source and holds 620 bottles of safety stock.

panel.heading: Score each risk: likelihood x impact

say: Hibiscus and sugar price rises each score 12, so she plans for them, for example buying hibiscus earlier when prices are lower.

panel.heading: Score each risk: likelihood x impact

say: The printer risk scores 6, and she fixes it today in five minutes by saving her own copy of the file.

say: Work on your highest risk first. In the first 15 days, find at least three possible suppliers and send your spec. Up to day 30, test samples against your reference.

items: Days 61 to 80: split orders, build stock
Days 81 to 90: review and choose next risk

say: Up to day 60, place real orders and measure lead time. Then split regular orders, for example 70% main and 30% backup.

say: To remember. Buy direct only when volume, cash and space allow. Share group transport by weight. Agree the Incoterm in writing.
Separate ordering, receiving and paying. And act first on your highest risk.
